title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation timeouts
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Tuned continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness and prevent starvation; added configurable starvation timeouts and metrics; rollout via 10% canary.
description: Motivation: customers and internal canaries showed that under mixed-latency workloads the continuous batcher scheduler occasionally starves lower-priority queues and increases p99 latency for small interactive requests. This PR tunes the scheduler queueing policy to improve fairness while preserving high throughput. Summary of changes: 1) introduce per-queue aging weights and a configurable starvation_timeout to force promotion when a queue has waited beyond the threshold; 2) change queue selection from pure size-based scoring to a hybrid score = weight * (1 + age_factor) which rewards older requests; 3) add soft and hard timeouts for pinned low-latency requests so they bypass batching after a short wait; 4) expose new knobs in config: scheduler.weight_decay, scheduler.starvation_timeout_ms, scheduler.max_bypass_rate; 5) add end-to-end and perf tests and dashboards; 6) update docs and Ops runbook with tuning guidance. Commits summary: - feat(scheduler): add aging weights and hybrid scoring - perf(scheduler): optimize queue scoring hot path and reduce allocations - test: add e2e fairness test and synthetic perf harness - docs: scheduler tuning guide and linear links Context & motivation: ENG-3145 tracked customer regressions where prioritizing throughput caused tail latency degradation for interactive client requests. The change is conservative: default behavior maintains previous throughput for homogeneous workloads but reduces starvation for mixed workloads. Tests & results: Microbenchmarks using our perf harness (mixed workload: 80% long sequences, 20% short interactive) show p99 for short requests improved from 420ms -> 170ms on xP4 configuration while aggregate throughput dropped <2%. End-to-end canary on staging (10% traffic) showed stable error/throughput and no regressions in KV cache hit rates. Files changed (high-level): pkg/continuous_batcher/scheduler.go, pkg/continuous_batcher/queue_manager.go, pkg/continuous_batcher/config.go, internal/bench/perf_fairness.py, tests/continuous_batcher/test_fairness.py, docs/ops/scheduler-tuning.md, dashboards/scheduler-fairness.json, ci/perf-checks.yml, examples/scheduler-configs/fairness.yaml, scripts/canary_deploy.sh, third_party/bench/readme.md, tools/metrics/emit_starvation_metric.go Review and conversation: - Jonas: "Can we keep the default starvation_timeout high enough to avoid bypassing batching for normal workloads?" Author: "Yes — default is 5s; added unit tests to assert default preserved behavior. Config exposed so SRE can tune per-cluster." - Priya: "Please add a metric for forced_bypass_count and a circuit-breaker when bypass rate > max_bypass_rate." Author: "Added metric and config max_bypass_rate with alert suggestions in runbook." - Lina: "Concern about additional allocations in hot path." Author: "Optimized scoring path and added microbench; allocations reduced to baseline." CI and checks: unit tests (PASS), integration e2e fairness test (PASS), perf benchmark (PASS with improved p99 in harness), lint/static analysis (PASS), canary smoke (PASS). Merge details: approved by reviewers, CI green, merged via squash on 2026-03-01. Rollout plan: 10% staging canary -> 50% -> full after 48h if no regressions. Backout: revert head branch; ops runbook includes steps and alert thresholds. Related: ENG-3153 covers follow-up telemetry for finer-grained queue metrics.
